name: Scales, modes and melody writing (mode colour, motifs, phrasing)
goal: Choose a scale/mode for the mood (Lydian bright -> Phrygian dark), use the characteristic note, and write motifs with call-and-response and rule-of-three phrasing.

source.note: Written from established production practice to fill a library gap; no single source video.

sources.title: Decode ACTION CUES with Melodic Cells
3 Simple Tricks for Beautiful Ambient Melodies

theory: Modes of the major scale share notes but change the tonal centre; each has a characteristic degree (Lydian #4, Dorian natural 6, Phrygian b2, Mixolydian b7). Pentatonics remove semitones for safe melodies.
prerequisites: DAW or the numpy renderer in sample-lab

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: Rendered part or recipe following the workflow

constraints: Portable recipe; not affiliated with any vendor; do not copy factory presets or sample packs.
Numbers in variants come from the source video transcripts; workflow steps are the consolidated mainstream practice.
Bring drums in early and avoid pitch wobble unless asked (user preferences from daily tests).

steps.action: Pick mood -> mode: Lydian dreamy, Ionian happy, Mixolydian bluesy, Dorian cool, Aeolian sad, Phrygian dark.
Emphasise the characteristic note on strong beats over a tonic drone.
Write a 1-2 bar motif using mostly steps with one leap; end phrases on chord tones.
Repeat motif twice, vary the third time (rhythm or ending).
Call and response between two instruments; keep melody in its own register.
For generative melodies lock to scale/pentatonic and limit range.
Hear the theory: run `/home/box/audio-tools/bin/python sample-lab/theory/scales_modes.py` from the repo root and compare the sections; reuse its functions as a starting point for renders.
steps.expect: WAV in sample-lab/theory/out/ demonstrating the principle

verification: Render a short test and A/B against a reference at matched loudness
Run the generator and confirm it writes a WAV without error
Check mono compatibility and that no element masks the kick/bass

variants.name: Action/tension cue from melodic cells: build short rhythmic-melodic cells, reorder and transpose them (up minor thirds for tension), repeat them so they sound intentional, put tension in the bass against a tonic ostinato, release with major triads, and derive octatonic (diminished) chords by cycling the cell down half steps
variants.goal: Write a short tense cue without a long melody: derive short melodic cells (a few pitches with a fixed interval shape) from a main ostinato, re-voice them in new orders and rhythms, transpose them up by minor thirds to raise tension, repeat cells so fast ideas sound deliberate, fix a simple non-random form, add tension by moving the bass against the ostinato's tonic and release it with major triads over the minor music, and add darker colour by blending the minor scale with the octatonic scale obtained by playing the cell four times each a half step lower.
steps: Write the main ostinato and pull out its pitch set (e.g. 4 notes). Write new cells from the same pitches in a different order and rhythm for another voice (e.g. horn).
Reduce a cell to its interval shape and transpose it; for tension move it up by minor thirds in a higher voice (strings).
Repeat the cells often enough that each fast idea is heard as deliberate; choose a simple form and stick to it.
Recontextualise on repeats: change the bass under the ostinato so it fights the ostinato's strong tonic (tension); to release, put major triads over the heavily minor ostinato.

Derive the octatonic scale: play the cell four times in a row, each starting a half step lower; the collected pitches form a diminished (octatonic) scale. Blend it with the minor scale (shared notes) and borrow its clashes for tension chords; space a semitone clash into a major 7th so it sounds intentional.
Optionally alternate between octatonic collections for major/minor triads over the ostinato to get ambiguous, uneasy colour.

variants.name: Three ambient-piano melody devices: a vector melody (one-direction Dorian scale run that may start and end on a dissonant 9th/11th), a classical sequence (a short phrase stepped down one scale degree at a time over chords that all keep one common tone in the bass), and modal transformation (two chord tones slip up a half step, maj7 -> min7 -> maj7, and the melody switches Lydian -> Dorian -> Lydian while the harmony keeps rising)
variants.goal: Write ambient melodies that tell a story without wobble or randomness, using three named devices from the source: (1) VECTOR melody: a plain scale run in one direction (down, up, or horizontal as a repeated two-note figure), e.g. E Dorian descending over Em6 -> Em7 inner-voice motion, allowed to start on the 9th (F#) and end on the 11th (A) because the motion justifies the dissonance; repeat it from a new start note over a new chord (e.g. from high A over an A chord) and return. (2) SEQUENCE: a short melodic ornament repeated one scale degree lower each time, over chords that share one bass tone placed on the offbeat (A under Dm/A -> Am7 -> Bbmaj7 -> A augmented -> A7, which resolves to D in the next section). (3) MODAL TRANSFORMATION (neo-Riemannian-style common-tone moves): Gbmaj7 with a Gb Lydian melody -> slip two notes up a half step to Gm7 (Bb and F stay) and play G Dorian -> slip its 3rd and 7th up a half step to Gmaj7 and play G Lydian -> keep going (Am7 -> Amaj7), adjusting the melody to each new mode.
steps: Set up the accompaniment: a repeating E minor pattern whose only change is one inner voice moving a step (Em6 -> Em7, C# -> D). Put a quiet pad under the piano and add reverb.
Vector melody: play a simple E Dorian scale descending over the bed. Try starting it on the 9th (F#) and ending on the 11th (A) so it begins and ends on bitey tones (Em69 colour).
Repeat the same scale shape from a new start note over a new chord (e.g. from high A over an A chord instead of E minor), then return to where you started.
Sequence: write a short melodic ornament (a few notes) and repeat it, moving it down one scale degree each time, two or three times.

Under the sequence, keep one common tone in the bass on the offbeat: Dm with A in the bass -> Am7 -> Bbmaj7 (A is its major 7th) -> A augmented -> A7 (the two upper notes step down). Let A7 (V of D) resolve to D at the next section.
Modal transformation: play Gbmaj7 (Gb Bb Db F) with a Gb Lydian melody (raised 4th, C).
Slip two notes up a half step (Gb -> G, Db -> D; Bb and F stay) to get Gm7, and re-fit the melody to G Dorian.

Now slip Gm7's 3rd and 7th up a half step (Bb -> B, F -> F#) to get Gmaj7, and play G Lydian. Continue the climb the same way (Am7 -> Amaj7 by raising the 3rd and 7th), adjusting the melody each time.
